sources.title: Gender Responsive Climate Security Assessment for Sri Lanka
sources.organization: UN Women; United Nations Development Programme (UNDP); UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA); Adelphi Research
sources.temporal_coverage: Field assessment published 30 September 2025; district-specific recommendations are proposals, not later outcomes.
sources.methodology: Gender-responsive climate-security assessment using district hotspot selection, field research and stakeholder consultation.
sources.limitations: The official PDF download returned 403; claims use only official indexed excerpts and the UN publication page. No uninspected passages are asserted.

sources.title: Remarks by the UN Resident Coordinator Marc-André Franche at the Launch of the Gender Responsive Climate Security Assessment
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Sri Lanka
sources.temporal_coverage: UN launch remarks delivered 1 October 2025, drawing on the assessment and reported local examples.
sources.methodology: UN speech summarizing assessment findings and local examples.
sources.limitations: Reported examples; no incidence estimates or impact evaluation.

sources.title: Cyclone Ditwah Situation Report: Sri Lanka, 8 December 2025-28 January 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) Sri Lanka
sources.temporal_coverage: Cyclone Ditwah emergency and early recovery reporting from 8 December 2025 to 28 January 2026.
sources.methodology: UNFPA report using DMC figures, needs assessments, safety audits and response data.
sources.limitations: Time-specific estimates and agency outputs; some cited risk methods were not independently reviewed.

sources.title: Implementation of Strategic Frameworks for Science-Driven Disaster Resilience - Tropical Cyclonic Storm Ditwah
sources.organization: Office of the Cabinet of Ministers, Government of Sri Lanka
sources.temporal_coverage: Cabinet press briefing dated 9 March 2026 on decisions and recommendations following Cyclone Ditwah in November 2025.
sources.methodology: Official Cabinet press briefing summarizing a post-disaster institutional research-needs exercise and approved resilience proposals.
sources.limitations: The page labels the briefing subject to confirmation at the next meeting; it describes approved proposals, not implementation or evaluated results.

claims.locator: PDF printed p.15, district-level hotspot selection table
claims.paraphrase: The assessment selected Mullaitivu and Batticaloa as post-conflict districts with high displacement and destruction; it describes climate-sensitive agriculture and fishing in Mullaitivu and heat, flood and drought exposure in Batticaloa.
claims.limitations: The table explains hotspot selection and co-located conflict/climate vulnerabilities; it does not say climate caused the earlier civil conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report jointly identifies conflict displacement and climate-sensitive livelihoods in these selected post-conflict districts.

claims.locator: PDF printed p.106, district-specific recommendations for Mullaitivu
claims.paraphrase: For Mullaitivu, the assessment proposes community water storage and climate-resilient farming, targeted support for women-headed households, transparent resource allocation, and participatory planning with marginalized Tamil and Muslim communities.
claims.limitations: These are district-specific recommendations, not evidence of funded or completed measures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The assessment recommends conflict-sensitive adaptation to address perceived inequity and strengthen trust among marginalized communities.

claims.locator: Speech, paragraphs on Mullaitivu land pressure and climate change
claims.paraphrase: The speaker says Muslim family returns increased Mullaitivu land pressure; military land-use disputes fuel resentment, while climate change shrinks arable land and intensifies competition.
claims.limitations: No quantified trends or causal estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate change explicitly worsens conflict-related land competition.

claims.locator: Speech, paragraph on education disruption in Batticaloa
claims.paraphrase: The speech says seasonal floods keep poor girls out of school for weeks in Batticaloa, heightening early-marriage and forced-labour risks.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Flood disruption is linked to protection risks.

claims.locator: Speech, paragraphs on Eastern Province resource allocation and trust
claims.paraphrase: Eastern Province farmers reportedly perceive water and subsidies as favouring southern and central provinces; the speaker warns ignored grievances can weaken national unity.

claims.locator: Speech, paragraph on shared preparedness in Mullaitivu
claims.paraphrase: Mullaitivu residents from Tamil, Muslim and Sinhala communities reportedly join community disaster preparedness, which the speaker presents as a path to reconciliation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Shared green action can bridge divides.

claims.locator: PDF pp.1-2/7, displacement, estate-sector concentration and Badulla landslide risk
claims.paraphrase: By 25 January 2026, UNFPA reported 165,884 people staying with hosts, concentrated in estate-sector Badulla, Kandy, Kegalle, Matale and Nuwara Eliya; nearly 68 percent of Badulla had landslide risk.
claims.limitations: January 2026 snapshot; Badulla risk attributed to NBRO.

claims.locator: PDF pp.1-2/7, shelter conditions and gender-based violence risk
claims.paraphrase: UNFPA says shelter crowding, poor lighting, limited privacy and shared sanitation raised gender-based violence risks for girls, older women and people with disabilities; road damage constrained aid access.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNFPA says shelter conditions elevate GBV risk.

claims.locator: PDF pp.2-3/7, safety audits and services
claims.paraphrase: UNFPA and government partners audited shelters in Badulla, Kegalle, Kandy and Matale, finding WASH, privacy, security and access gaps; response included SRH/GBV services, supplies and cash.
institutions: Ministry of Women and Child Affairs
claims.limitations: Agency-reported outputs; service and funding gaps persisted.

claims.locator: Cabinet press briefing, Ditwah climate stress test and resilience-framework decision
claims.paraphrase: The Cabinet briefing calls Cyclone Ditwah a climate stress test exposing systemic infrastructure vulnerabilities and reports approval of a shift from reactive response and recovery toward a science-driven proactive resilience framework, informed by institutional research-needs recommendations.
claims.limitations: The Cabinet site says the briefing was subject to confirmation; framework approval does not demonstrate implementation or outcomes.

access_audit.locator: Official indexed PDF excerpts from printed p.15 (hotspot selection) and p.106 (Mullaitivu recommendations); official publication page inspected.
access_audit.notes: Direct PDF endpoint returned 403. Claims use only the official search-indexed excerpts; the landing page verifies publisher, title, date and four-district scope.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full official speech inspected, especially paragraphs on Mullaitivu land and climate pressures, Batticaloa education, resource allocation and shared preparedness.
access_audit.notes: Speech reproduces reported examples; its claims are not treated as independent prevalence or impact estimates.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 7-page UNFPA Situation Report, 8 December 2025-28 January 2026; displacement, shelter-protection risks, access, safety audits and response passages inspected.
access_audit.notes: Report incorporates DMC and NBRO information and partner-reported service outputs; cited risk values retain their attribution.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Complete Cabinet press briefing on the science-driven resilience framework and post-Ditwah recommendations.
access_audit.notes: Page labels the briefing subject to confirmation at the next Cabinet meeting; proposals are not treated as implemented results.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

search_audit.query: Sri Lanka district climate-security assessment, post-conflict Northern and Eastern provinces, local rainfall, flood, drought and livelihood vulnerability
search_audit.outcome: UN field assessment excerpts identify climate-sensitive livelihoods in post-conflict Mullaitivu and Batticaloa; a full UNFPA report adds estate-sector displacement and Badulla landslide risk after Ditwah.

search_audit.query: Sri Lanka primary source climate change land disputes, post-conflict grievances, gender, resource allocation and peace mediators
search_audit.outcome: The UN Resident Coordinator directly links climate-driven land pressure with unresolved military land-use disputes and resentment, and identifies flood-related school disruption and perceived resource-allocation inequity as protection and trust concerns.

search_audit.query: Sri Lanka conflict or governance barriers to climate adaptation, land and water allocation, disaster response official evidence
search_audit.outcome: The UN speech documents unresolved military land-use disputes and perceptions of inequitable water and subsidy allocation; reviewed sources do not establish that conflict obstructed a named adaptation project. UNFPA documents shelter and access constraints during disaster response.

search_audit.query: Sri Lanka inclusive climate adaptation, inter-community disaster preparedness, protection response and post-Ditwah resilience capacity official sources
search_audit.outcome: UN sources report shared community preparedness in Mullaitivu and early-recovery protection and health actions; Cabinet reports an approved proactive resilience framework and research recommendations, but implementation is not yet evidenced.

gaps: The climate-security assessment PDF was not directly accessible; specific report claims rely only on official indexed excerpts. The separate UN speech was inspected in full.
The UN speech gives source-stated local pathways but not quantified trends, causal effect estimates or measured outcomes; farmer allocation concerns are reported perceptions, not an allocation audit.
The UNFPA Ditwah report is an early-recovery snapshot through 28 January 2026; shelter protection concerns and service gaps are not measures of longer-term outcomes.

No reviewed source evaluates whether insecurity prevented delivery of a named climate-adaptation intervention; the Cabinet resilience framework remains a proposal/approval rather than evaluated implementation.
